article.body:
While standing in my dining room, John Adler explained, “My father was a very sad, broken man. He had gone through so many painful experiences. However, the last year of his life was very different. My father was—happy! I had no idea where the happiness came from, but I welcomed the change with open arms. The glow on his face was indescribable.”

“Over time,” John continued, “I noticed that Friday had

become my father’s favorite day of the week; not because it

meant ‘no work until Monday,’ but because he really looked forward to being at the store on Fridays. Until a few minutes ago, I never understood why he found such enjoyment in going to work every Friday. Finally, today, it all became clear. I found the missing piece of the puzzle. You, Sruli, were the highlight of his week! I stayed to thank you for lighting up my father’s life when he needed it most. “

And just like that, John Adler walked out the door.

Once again, it was Friday, and I was sitting on a bumpy Manhattan-bound 3 train heading to my Mivtzoim route. I thought of the thousands of children who had just become chayolim by joining Hashem’s army. A question came to mind: “It’s now 30 days before my favorite Yom Tov. How are all these chayolim going to help spread the light of Chanukah?”

I lifted my head and noticed the many ads lining the walls of the train. B’hashgocho protis, the

much discussion, an agreement was made: I would provide the funds, and he (the head of Tzivos Hashem) would make it all happen! A graphic designer was hired to design campaign ads and a website.

The campaign’s slogan was, ‘Got Glow? Visit our website to order your free Menorah in time for Chanukah 2022.’ I took the word “glow” from the lips of John Adler when he had described his father’s shining face. Pretty neat, huh?

The week before Chanukah, hundreds of NYC buses and subways were transformed into ‘shluchim on wheels.’ From Broadway to Brighton Beach, the ads reminded New Yorkers of the upcoming Festival of Lights. More importantly, the ads publicized our free menorah offer, enabling thousands of people to light their very own menorahs over Chanukah.

With the help of Merkos, every Shliach participating in the ‘Got Glow?’ campaign received $1,000 for his Chanukah program.

Tzivos Hashem bases around the world were bustling. Chayolim gathered together to pack thousands of Glow Kits to be shipped to the Jewish people in their state or country. Each kit included a tin Menorah, a dreidel, a bag of chocolate coins, candles, and a card with the brochos for Chanukah.

Back home, the doorbell did not stop ringing. At first, bochurim from Oholei Torah arrived. They asked if I would sponsor one of the two buses that they needed for Chanukah visitations to Jewish homes and apartment buildings. I told them that with Rafi’s money, I

would sponsor four buses; so long as each OT Bochur would agree to take a chayol of Tzivos Hashem with him on Mivtzoim. There was one more requirement: all four buses had to have ‘Got Glow?’ ads plastered onto them.

At 7 pm, the head of the Mitzvah Tanks rang my bell. He asked me to sponsor this year’s additional tanks. I told him that I’d double the amount of tanks they had last year if every bochur would agree to take a chayol with him on the tank, and of course the tanks would have to carry the ‘Got Glow?’ banners on them.

8 pm, Rabbi Gerlitzky, in charge of mivtzoim in hospitals and nursing homes, knocked on the door. “I’m sorry to bother you, Rabbi Mendelsohn, but I’m looking for your son, Sruli. Is he possibly home?”

“Say no more, Rabbi Gerlitzky. I’m all in for sponsoring extra buses for your mivtzoim, so long as the high school girls take our young chayolos with them on their visits.”

Bochurim from Lubavitch Yeshivah came with their pitched at around 9 pm.

“We’re making car menorahs. Is it possible for you to spon—“

“I want at least 770 cars in the parade this year. You make them, I’ll pay for them. Every car gets a large ‘Got Glow?’ magnet on it.”

Wherever you looked, you saw the words ‘Got Glow?’ So it came as little surprise that the NY Times picked up on the story, and wrote an article about it a few days before Chanukah. It was great because we got extra publicity for the website. During Chanukah

itself, the campaign was mentioned on the radio several times. All the news anchors started the exact same way: “New York City is glowing this Hanukah, thanks to a group of children from Crown Heights…

Chanukah 2022—SMASHING SUCCESS! In total, we sent 180,000 Glow kits all over the world.

The day after Chanukah, I sat in my room and thought about all that had taken place. I wonder if Rafi ever imagined that he would sponsor one of the biggest Chanukah Mivtzah Campaigns that the city had ever seen. There wasn’t much left of the money that he gave me.
